title: Minnich Road NB / SB over I-469 | proposed 2026 rehabilitation
source_note: INDOT B-44533, 62-sheet July 31 2026 proposed rehabilitation, November 2026 letting. This is a proposed design, not a completed construction or verified present-day model.
assumptions: Exterior visualization reconstruction, not an as-built survey, load rating or validated FEM mesh.
No internal reinforcement, prestressing strands, embedded studs, weld beads or fabrication holes. Material colors are visualization choices.
Source pages mix historical removals and proposed work. Only the explicitly named design state is modeled; the separately stored later references do not alter that state.
Buried foundations are hidden by default. Unknown driven pile lengths, terrain and approach-road terminal systems are omitted.
Bearing contact checks verify constructed geometric attachment only; they do not establish surveyed bearing elevations or fabrication tolerances.
Eight girder lines represent two NBI structures in one crossing; the new continuous deck intentionally eliminates the longitudinal joint (sheet 20).
Intermediate columns and caps are provisional envelopes. Original substructure plans are unavailable. No foundations were invented.
Middle-span flange changes and exact end-span taper/upper kink remain simplified; this model is not suitable for FEM without a separate source reconciliation.

End-span depth transitions, sixteen field-splice envelopes, stiffeners and representative bracing. Exact retained flange schedule, upper-flange kink, camber and K-frame detail remain incomplete.
Forty bearing envelopes; S5-B end pads represented. Retained intermediate shoes and exact source shim-seat reconciliation are incomplete.
Support envelopes only: original substructure plans were absent from the public package. Column arrangement and dimensions must not be used for analysis or quantity takeoff.
FC rails and six RCBA panels. Detailed wingwall, TFC/guardrail transitions, stepped approach edge offsets and drainage are unfinished.
Unknown foundations, road/site surfaces, drainage troughs, guardrail terminals, all connection holes and full retained substructure details.
